newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia forecasts '97 oil output at 691,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia forecasts '97 oil output at 691,000 bpd.

text.p: Malaysia's production of crude oil, including condensates, will fall next year to an average of 691,000 barrels per day (bpd), against an estimated 706,000 bpd in 1996, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
In its 1996/97 Economic Report issued on Friday, the ministry did not say why production would fall by 2.1 percent between this year and 1997. Output in 1995 was 705,400 bpd.
In 1996, crude oil production is estimated at about 630,000 bpd, while oil recovered from natural gas production -- also called condensates -- would be 76,000 bpd, the ministry said.
Natural gas production in 1996 would surge an estimated 22.4 percent to 3,475 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscf/d) against 2,839 mmscf/d last year.
The report also forecast the average global crude oil price would fall to $18.50 a barrel in 1997 from an estimated $20.0 this year, and against $18.30 in 1995.
The ministry did not explain the reasons which led to its lower price forecast for next year.
The 13 oil fields off Peninsular Malaysia are expected to contribute 58.5 percent of total oil production this year.
Sarawak's 13 fields are estimated to contribute 32.2 percent and Sabah's seven fields the remaining 9.3 percent.
